page: Amazon Web Services c8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz, each core features 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, alongside a shared 36 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. This instance does not include local storage or graphics processing units.

Benchmark data highlights the server's exceptional multi-threaded capabilities. It achieves top-tier performance in multi-core processing, software compilation, and ray tracing, as evidenced by its high scores in stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory performance is also in the top tier, with uncached read bandwidth reaching 909.22 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 404.46 GB/sec. Single-core performance, including single-threaded compression and text processing, falls within the average range. The server demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations and Redis SET operations, processing 353.35 million operations per second. However, text generation for large language models remains a bottleneck, with performance scaling poorly on smaller models.

The bare-metal architecture of the c8g.metal-48xl offers high resource density and eliminates hypervisor overhead, making it highly cost-efficient for highly parallelized, CPU-bound workloads. The lack of bundled local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This server is highly suited for large-scale software compilation, high-throughput static web serving, distributed database operations, and multi-threaded scientific simulations.
